claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the mandatory timing requirement that an employee must provide notice as soon as practicable when the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable.
The claim correctly reflects the general expectation regarding practicability of notice within the timeframe of usual employer requirements.
The claim correctly reflects the permission for a spokesperson to give notice when the employee is unable to do so personally, along with the listed illustrative examples.
The claim correctly captures the exemption illustrated by an emergency room visit for a child's severe asthma attack.
The claim faithfully reflects the source example of prompt notice expected after administering an inhaler at home.
The claim correctly extracts the core requirement under 29 CFR 825.303(b) that an employee provide sufficient information for an employer to determine FMLA applicability.
The claim accurately lists the situational types of information that may satisfy sufficient notice, preserving logical grouping and qualifications.
The claim accurately states the rule that an employee seeking leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason need not expressly assert or mention FMLA rights.
The claim accurately represents the affirmative duty when seeking leave for a previously provided qualifying reason to specifically reference either the reason or the need for FMLA leave.
The claim accurately captures the threshold rule that calling in sick without more information does not trigger employer FMLA obligations.
The claim accurately captures the expectation that employers obtain additional required info informally.
The claim properly reflects an employee's mandatory obligation to respond to employer questions designed to determine FMLA eligibility.
The claim correctly reflects the consequence of failing to respond to employer inquiries.
The claim correctly extracts the requirement to follow usual and customary procedures absent unusual circumstances for unforeseeable leave.
The claim captures the employer's permission to require calling a designated number or individual, while also incorporating the broader context of section (c).
The claim accurately states the emergency medical treatment exemption from call-in procedures until stabilized and capable of using a phone.
The claim accurately reflects the source statement that advance written notice may not be required in an emergency requiring FMLA leave.
The claim accurately captures the consequence that failure to comply with usual procedural requirements without justification may result in delay or denial of FMLA leave.
